The dominant edge class that actually survives evidence in this tier is the international-standards bridge (SNA, BPM6, MFSMCG, ISIC, ICLS, e-GDDS, SDDS) — these countries' own statistical sites are thin on compilation methodology but do state which manual they follow. Domestic data chains (national accounts using industrial/agricultural/oil output as inputs, budget deficit from budget execution, NPLs from banking-system reporting) were looked for repeatedly across all seven countries and are almost entirely UNDOCUMENTED on the publishers' own sites — see `_dropped`, which is longer than `dependencies` and is the more informative half of this slice. THREE EDGES WERE DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED despite agents proposing them: Vietnam's VSIC→ISIC link (only third-party evidence, classification.codes, not a primary source), and Iraq's oil-revenue→oil-exports and federal-budget→oil-revenue chain (evidence was a secondary analyst PDF citing Budget Law 13 of 2023 by article number, not the law itself — a good lead, recorded in `_dropped`). reports.title: Household Income and Expenditure Survey (HIES), Myanmar
reports.publisher: Central Statistical Organization (CSO), Ministry of Planning and Finance
reports.description: Minted so that Myanmar's CPI has a real source node rather than an edge to the CSO institutional core, which would have been a publisher relationship wearing a dependency's clothes. Quote re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session — the researching agent had paraphrased it as "Household Income and Expenditure Survey generates weights in computing Consumer Price Index (CPI)", which is the same fact in words the page does not use.

GSO's article on the 2017 centralisation of GRDP compilation states the problem it was solving — "there is a difference of over 1.7 times between the sum of GRDP of 63 provinces and centrally-run cities and the national gross domestic product (GDP)" — and the arrangement that replaced local self-calculation: "Since 2017, the MPI (GSO) shall compile and announce GRDP; provincial statistical offices of central-affiliated cities and provinces shall be responsible for collecting the input information in their provinces or cities and reporting to the MPI (GSO)," described as "a solution to narrow the increasing difference between GDP and GRDP like at the present." Provincial GRDP is therefore compiled by the national-accounts compiler and bound to the national GDP figure. All three quotes re-fetched and confirmed verbatim by the orchestrating session; the researching agent had found only the middle one.

_dropped.why: CAUGHT BY THE VALIDATOR AT MINT TIME, AND THE VALIDATOR WAS RIGHT. This round originally minted mm-national-accounts -> sna-1993 AND -> sna-2008 off a single CSO sentence: "it is also intended to use the GDP calculation when the method of 93 SNA, 2008 SNA is used" (csostat.gov.mm/AboutCSO/StatisticalSystem, re-verified verbatim by the orchestrating session). `npm run validate` then flagged that a pre-existing _dropped note in ph-vn-th-mm-wiring-grok-2026-08.json describes that exact edge — and reading that note is what settled the question. It records IMF metadata for Myanmar reading: "Myanmar's NA broadly follows the concepts and definitions of the System of National Accounts 1968. Consequently, changes introduced by the 1993 SNA/2008 SNA affecting GDP are being implemented." That does not contradict the CSO sentence, it EXPLAINS it: CSO says "intended to use", the metadata says "being implemented", and both mean Myanmar's actual current basis is the 1968 SNA with 93/2008 in progress. A methodology_depends_on edge to sna-1993 or sna-2008 would assert an adopted basis that neither source asserts, so both edges were withdrawn before landing. RESOLUTION PATH, and it is now easy: `sna-1968` DOES exist as a live node in the corpus. The earlier note's blocker — "target id 'sna-1993' is NOT present in the live corpus" — is also now stale; sna-1993, sna-1968, sna-2008 and sna-2025 all exist. What is still needed is a Myanmar-side or non-DSBB source for the 1968 basis, since this project does not cite the IMF DSBB. Mint mm-national-accounts -> sna-1968 once that is in hand, and mark the older note resolved at the same time. MODELLING QUESTION FOR THOMAS, not a research failure. SCI's national-accounts page does state "Classification of individual consumption by purpose (COICOP), for classification of household final consumption expenditures" — verified verbatim by the orchestrating session. But it names COICOP with no revision, and the corpus has only revision-specific nodes: `un-coicop-2018` and `un-coicop-hbs-1999`. Wiring a source that says 'COICOP' to the 2018 edition asserts an edition the document does not assert, and Iran's accounts are on the SNA 1993 vintage, which makes a pre-2018 COICOP the more likely referent. Not minted. The fix is a decision, not more research: either mint a revision-neutral `un-coicop` parent node that the revisions hang off, or accept that generic-COICOP citations cannot be wired at all.

Same modelling question as the Iran entry above, and the reason Iraq ended this round with two edges instead of three. Iraq's CSO CPI bulletin for May 2018 does state its 486 sampled items are "distributed on 12 divisions according to Classification Of Individual Consumption by Purpose briefly COICOP" — a good primary quote — but again names no revision, and a bulletin published in 2018 is more likely to mean the pre-2018 edition than the one released that year. Held for the same decision.

CONTRADICTION FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED — this needs Thomas's ruling, and it is the reason Iran contributed one edge to this round instead of seven. The edge ir-national-accounts -> sna-2008 is ALREADY LIVE in the corpus. But SCI's own current English national-accounts page says something else, verbatim and re-verified by the orchestrating session: "Theoretically, regional accounts, just like national accounts, follow the latest revision of the system of national accounts SNA 93." The UN Statistics Division's Iran country record independently lists "National Accounts Methodology 1993 System of National Accounts", which favours SNA 93 too. Per PLAYBOOK rule 13, a fresh well-verified finding that contradicts a live edge does not automatically win: the live sna-2008 edge is caveated here rather than deleted, and the new SNA-93 claim is deferred rather than minted. SIX EDGES ARE HELD PENDING THIS RULING — ir-national-accounts -> sna-1993 and the five ir-grdp-* -> sna-1993 edges, all resting on that one SCI sentence, which covers regional accounts explicitly ("regional accounts, just like national accounts"). Minting them while the sna-2008 edge stands would have left the corpus asserting both vintages for Iran with nothing flagging it. The one Iran edge that WAS minted, ir-national-accounts -> isic, is independent of this dispute. Counter-evidence for the live edge: a 2015 UN workshop slide filed under Iran's country folder states "Quarterly National Accounts cover the entire sequence of accounts and balance sheets in the 2008 SNA" — but it may be describing the framework generically for training, and it is a decade old.

ZERO EDGES, and the zero is the finding. Yemen's own primary statistical documentation is effectively unreachable in 2026. cso-yemen.com fails to load (robots.txt error, HTTP 500) — effectively dead. The single most substantive Yemen-specific document reached was the UN Statistics Division's national-accounts country record (unstats.un.org/Unsd/nationalaccount/cInfo.asp?cID=887), and it RULES OUT rather than supports the obvious edges: it states "National Accounts Methodology 1968 System of National Accounts", base year 1990, last UN-NAQ submission 2008, with a '2008 SNA Implementation Programme' listed only as an aspirational ISWGNA initiative. So no SNA 1993 or SNA 2008 edge can honestly be minted — Yemen is on the 1968 SNA, and this corpus has an `sna-1968` node, which is the lead for a later round. The Central Bank of Yemen's site (centralbank.gov.ye) does load and appears genuine (exchange-rate newsletter, public debt sections) but exposed no balance-of-payments report or methodology page. The 2004 census, Yemen's last, could not be verified: the IHSN catalog record failed twice and the GHDx record is a bare stub. Everything else search surfaces is third-party aggregators (CEIC, FRED, Moody's), which cannot substantiate a methodology edge.

ZERO EDGES, and again the zero is the finding. cbssyr.sy — the Central Bureau of Statistics domain — failed on every variant tried (http://www.cbssyr.sy/, https://cbssyr.sy/, http://cbssyr.sy), each at the robots.txt fetch stage with a connection timeout, i.e. the host is not responding rather than blocking. INSTITUTIONAL CHANGE WORTH RECORDING: the CBS appears no longer to exist as an independent body — it was merged into the General Authority for Planning and International Cooperation, renamed the Syrian Planning and Statistics Commission under Decree No. 27 of 2025 (per Wikipedia, not yet confirmed against a primary Syrian source). cb.gov.sy (Central Bank of Syria) IS reachable and lists real report titles — Balance of Payments indicators, IIP, exchange-rate bulletins, monetary survey, government account indicators — but every page fetched was a navigation index or department description, never the underlying report, so no methodology sentence could be quoted. Also notable: GHDx's catalog of Syrian statistical history lists a 1976 census and various MICS rounds but does NOT list a 2004 census, which quietly undercuts the widely-cited '2004 census' as the population denominator. Next round should search the Syrian Planning and Statistics Commission by name and by Decree 27 of 2025.
